key_insight: Solaris extends action-conditioned video world models from single-agent, single-view settings to realistic multiplayer environments by learning to generate consistent, synchronized multi-view observations.
problem_solved: Existing video world models fail to capture multi-agent interactions and consistent views across players; Solaris addresses the lack of datasets and models that can simulate realistic, synchronized multi-view gameplay (e.g., in Minecraft).
method: Design a multiplayer data collection system for robust, continuous, automated capture of multi-agent gameplay and synchronized camera views in game environments like Minecraft.
Train an action-conditioned video world model that models multi-agent dynamics and enforces cross-view consistency so generated videos remain coherent across players and viewpoints.
Use end-to-end training and temporal conditioning to predict future multi-view observations given past frames and agent actions.
impact: Solaris enables research and applications that require realistic multi-agent, multi-view simulation—improving planning, multi-agent RL, and video prediction in interactive 3D environments. Practitioners gain a scalable pipeline and model approach for building synchronized world models beyond single-player scenarios.

paper_title: Solaris: Building a Multiplayer Video World Model in Minecraft
paper_authors: Georgy Savva, Oscar Michel, Daohan Lu, Suppakit Waiwitlikhit, Timothy Meehan
